prompt.zh-TW: 你從停車場駛出，前方是一條雙向道路。日本一般應進入哪一側？
prompt.en: You leave a parking lot onto a two-way road. Which side should you enter in Japan?

explanation.zh-TW: 日本車輛靠左行駛；駛入雙向道路時應進入左側車道。
explanation.en: Vehicles drive on the left in Japan; enter the left side of a two-way road.

prompt.zh-TW: 紅燈時沒有綠色箭頭，但左邊沒有任何車或行人，可以左轉嗎？
prompt.en: At a red light with no green arrow, the road to the left is completely clear. May you turn left?

explanation.zh-TW: 紅燈不是自行判斷可轉彎的號誌；只有適用方向的綠色箭頭允許時才可通行。
explanation.en: A red light does not permit a turn based on your own judgment; proceed only when an applicable green arrow allows it.

prompt.zh-TW: 號誌剛變黃，你距離停止線仍足以平順安全停車。該怎麼做？
prompt.en: The signal turns yellow and you still have enough distance to stop safely. What should you do?

explanation.zh-TW: 仍能安全停車時，應在停止線前停下，不應為了搶黃燈而加速。
explanation.en: When you can stop safely, stop before the line rather than accelerating through the yellow signal.

prompt.zh-TW: 主燈紅燈，但亮起向右綠色箭頭，可以怎麼做？
prompt.en: The main signal is red, but a green right arrow is lit. What may you do?

text.zh-TW: 依箭頭方向右轉並持續注意衝突交通
text.en: Turn right as indicated while checking for conflicts
You may not move at all

explanation.zh-TW: 適用方向的綠色箭頭允許沿箭頭方向通行；仍須注意行人與其他衝突交通。
explanation.en: An applicable green arrow permits movement in its direction; continue checking for pedestrians and conflicting traffic.

prompt.zh-TW: 止まれ前車速降到約 2 km/h、左右看完但輪胎沒有完全停止，算完成停車嗎？
prompt.en: At a STOP sign you slow to about 2 km/h, look both ways, but the wheels never fully stop. Is that a complete stop?

explanation.zh-TW: 止まれ要求車輪完全停止；極慢滑行仍不是完整停車。
explanation.en: A STOP sign requires the wheels to stop completely; a very slow rolling stop is still not a complete stop.

prompt.zh-TW: 綠燈右轉時，對向有車直行。誰應先行？
prompt.en: You are turning right on green while an oncoming vehicle goes straight. Who has priority?

explanation.zh-TW: 右轉車應讓對向直行交通先行，確認安全後再完成右轉。
explanation.en: A right-turning vehicle yields to oncoming straight traffic and turns only after confirming it is safe.

prompt.zh-TW: 左轉前只要看右側來車即可，不必看車身左側。對或錯？
prompt.en: Before a left turn, it is enough to watch traffic from the right; there is no need to check the left side of your vehicle. True or false?

explanation.zh-TW: 左側可能有自行車、機車或行人；左轉前必須檢查車身左側與穿越區域。
explanation.en: Cyclists, motorcycles, or pedestrians may be on the left; check the vehicle's left side and crossing area before turning.

prompt.zh-TW: 斑馬線旁有行人面向道路等待，你應該：
prompt.en: A pedestrian is waiting at a crossing facing the road. You should:

text.zh-TW: 維持速度，等他踏上斑馬線再說
text.en: Maintain speed until the person steps onto it

text.zh-TW: 以能停住的速度接近，必要時停讓
text.en: Approach ready to stop and yield

explanation.zh-TW: 接近行人穿越道時應能安全停車；行人準備通行時必須停讓。
explanation.en: Approach a pedestrian crossing ready to stop, and yield when a pedestrian is about to cross.

prompt.zh-TW: 前車停在斑馬線前，你看不到有人，可以從旁邊繞過嗎？
prompt.en: A vehicle is stopped at a pedestrian crossing, but you cannot see a pedestrian. May you pass around it?

explanation.zh-TW: 前車可能正在讓行你看不到的行人；不得直接從旁超越。
explanation.en: The stopped vehicle may be yielding to a pedestrian you cannot see; do not pass around it.

prompt.zh-TW: 窄路通過自行車，無法留出約 1 公尺間隔時，最好的做法是：
prompt.en: On a narrow road you cannot leave about one meter while passing a cyclist. Best action:

text.en: Maintain speed and get past quickly

text.zh-TW: 明顯降速並保留可行的最大安全間隔
text.en: Slow significantly and leave the safest practical gap

explanation.zh-TW: 無法確保約 1 公尺時，警察廳安全目安要求明顯降速並保留可行的最大間隔。
explanation.en: When about one meter cannot be secured, NPA safety guidance calls for a marked speed reduction and the safest practical gap.

prompt.zh-TW: 「1 公尺、20–30 km/h」是所有情況固定不變的法定數字嗎？
prompt.en: Are “1 meter” and “20–30 km/h” fixed statutory numbers for every bicycle-passing situation?

text.zh-TW: 否，是警察廳提供的安全目安
text.en: No, they are NPA safety guidance

explanation.zh-TW: 這些數字是警察廳的安全目安，不是所有情況固定不變的法定門檻。
explanation.en: These figures are NPA safety guidance, not universal fixed statutory thresholds.

prompt.zh-TW: 道路標誌寫 40 km/h，但你認為這條路看起來可以開 60。最高應依哪個？
prompt.en: A road is posted at 40 km/h, but it looks safe for 60. Which limit controls?

explanation.zh-TW: 現場標示的 40 km/h 速限具有約束力，不能以主觀路況判斷提高到 60。
explanation.en: The posted 40 km/h limit controls; a driver cannot raise it to 60 based on personal judgment.

prompt.zh-TW: 2026-09-01 起，主要無中央線／車道線的生活道路，在沒有另行指定速限時要特別注意哪個法定速限？
prompt.en: From 2026-09-01, what statutory limit becomes especially important on many local roads without a center line or lane markings when no other limit is posted?

explanation.zh-TW: 自 2026-09-01 起，符合規定範圍的生活道路無另行指定時，法定速限降為 30 km/h。
explanation.en: From 2026-09-01, covered local roads without another posted limit use the new 30 km/h statutory limit.

prompt.zh-TW: 平交道柵欄開著，但出口因塞車沒有足夠位置容納你的車，可以先開進軌道區等待嗎？
prompt.en: A railway barrier is open, but traffic beyond the tracks leaves no room for your vehicle. May you enter and wait on the tracks?

explanation.zh-TW: 出口沒有足夠空間容納整輛車時，不得進入平交道軌道區。
explanation.en: Do not enter the tracks unless there is enough clear space beyond them for the whole vehicle.

prompt.zh-TW: 導航叫你右轉，但現場標誌禁止進入。應聽誰的？
prompt.en: Navigation tells you to turn, but a current road sign prohibits entry. Which do you follow?

explanation.zh-TW: 導航可能過時；現場道路標誌才是當下有效的交通管制。
explanation.en: Navigation may be outdated; the current road sign is the traffic control that applies on site.

prompt.zh-TW: 藍底紅框標誌上是紅色叉號（X），和只有一條紅斜線相比，限制更嚴格在哪裡？
prompt.en: A blue-and-red sign shows a red X rather than a single red slash. What makes the X stricter?

explanation.zh-TW: 紅色叉號是「駐停車禁止」，連上下客等臨時停車原則上也不能做；單斜線是「駐車禁止」。仍要一起看附加時段與箭頭。
explanation.en: The red X means no stopping or parking, so even temporary stopping is generally prohibited; the single slash means no parking. Also read any time panel and arrows.

prompt.zh-TW: 高速公路右側超車道前方沒車，可以一路待在右側嗎？
prompt.en: The right passing lane is empty. May you cruise in it continuously?

explanation.zh-TW: 右側是超車道；完成超車後應回到主要行車道，不應長時間占用。
explanation.en: The right lane is for passing; return to the main driving lane after overtaking rather than cruising there.

prompt.zh-TW: 租車沒有可用 ETC 卡，可以進 ETC 專用車道嗎？
prompt.en: Your rental car has no usable ETC card. May you enter an ETC-only lane?

explanation.zh-TW: 沒有可用 ETC 卡或相容設備時，應使用一般車道，不得進入 ETC 專用車道。
explanation.en: Without usable ETC, use a general toll lane and do not enter an ETC-only lane.

prompt.zh-TW: 剛錯過高速公路出口，最安全的做法是：
prompt.en: You just missed your expressway exit. Safest action:

text.zh-TW: 繼續前往下一個安全出口再重新規劃
text.en: Continue to the next safe exit and reroute

explanation.zh-TW: 不得倒車或停在分流處；應安全繼續到下一個出口後再重新規劃。
explanation.en: Do not reverse or stop at the split; continue safely to the next exit and reroute.

prompt.zh-TW: 日本加油站的「軽油」是什麼？
prompt.en: What does 軽油 mean at a Japanese fuel station?

explanation.zh-TW: 「軽油」是柴油，不是輕型車專用汽油；加油前仍應確認租車指定油種。
explanation.en: 軽油 means diesel, not gasoline for small cars; still confirm the rental vehicle's specified fuel.

prompt.zh-TW: 租來的車應加什麼油，最可靠的依據是：
prompt.en: The most reliable way to determine fuel for a rental car is:

text.zh-TW: 租車文件與車輛燃料標示
text.en: Rental instructions and vehicle fuel specification

explanation.zh-TW: 應依租車公司文件與車輛燃料標示確認，不能用車身大小猜測。
explanation.en: Use the rental instructions and vehicle fuel specification; do not guess from vehicle size.

prompt.zh-TW: 輕微擦撞、雙方都沒受傷，可以交換資料後直接離開嗎？
prompt.en: After a minor collision with no injuries, may both parties exchange details and simply leave?

explanation.zh-TW: 即使無人受傷且損害輕微，仍應向警察 110 報告事故。
explanation.en: Even when no one is injured and damage is minor, report the collision to police at 110.

prompt.zh-TW: 高速公路車輛故障停妥並做警示後，人留在車裡等救援比較安全。對或錯？
prompt.en: After an expressway breakdown and warning other traffic, it is safer to remain inside the vehicle while waiting. True or false?

explanation.zh-TW: 在安全可行的情況下，應離開車輛並撤到護欄外等較安全位置等待。
explanation.en: When it is safe to do so, leave the vehicle and wait in a safer place such as behind the guardrail.

prompt.zh-TW: 昨晚喝酒、今天早上仍有宿醉感，但沒有正在喝酒，可以開嗎？
prompt.en: You drank last night and still feel hungover this morning, but you are not currently drinking. Should you drive?

explanation.zh-TW: 仍有宿醉或可能受酒精影響時不應駕駛；隔夜不代表酒精影響已消失。
explanation.en: Do not drive while hungover or possibly affected by alcohol; overnight time does not guarantee the effect is gone.

prompt.zh-TW: 速限 40 km/h，前車開得更快，網路又說相機通常要超速很多才拍。你可以跟著加速嗎？
prompt.en: The limit is 40 km/h, the car ahead is faster, and an online post claims cameras trigger only far above the limit. May you speed up to follow?

text.zh-TW: 可以，沒到傳聞門檻就安全
text.en: Yes, staying below the rumoured threshold is safe

text.zh-TW: 不可以，40 是上限；取締方式不是超速額度
text.en: No. Forty is the limit; enforcement methods are not a speeding allowance

explanation.zh-TW: 日本有固定、半固定與可搬式速度取締。設備位置、取締方式或網路傳聞都不會提高現場速限；不要跟著前車超速。
explanation.en: Japan uses fixed, semi-fixed and portable speed enforcement. Equipment location, enforcement method and online rumours do not raise the posted limit; do not copy a speeding lead vehicle.
